analysis.title: CIO Weekly Commentary: Incoming opportunities with munis
key_insights: Q3 GDP advance estimate was +3.4% annualized, above consensus and up from +2.2% in the prior quarter, driven by consumer spending and surging business investment.

Growth is concentrated in two groups: AI-focused corporations investing in infrastructure, and affluent households benefiting from rising financial asset prices. Nuveen says this narrow base raises questions about sustainability.

September headline PCE price index accelerated to 3.6% y/y and core PCE reached 3.1%. Real disposable personal income fell -0.3% m/m while consumers kept spending, and household savings remain historically subdued.

The Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4.00%. The vote was divided, with two dissenters favoring additional tightening, unlike the unanimous July decision to hike. Chair Kevin Warsh said more work is needed on inflation.
Nuveen sees a likelihood of a Fed rate increase in December, with perhaps one or two more in 2027.

Alphabet reported extraordinary Q3 cloud growth but disappointing search and advertising results and negative free cash flow. Investors are questioning whether AI monetization can justify the capex and possible cannibalization of core businesses.
The Bloomberg Municipal Bond Index returned -6.35% in Q3, the worst quarter for munis since 1981. Nuveen attributes the losses mainly to rate dislocation, not credit deterioration.
Municipal yields were 4.21% for the overall market as of 30 October, in the 95th percentile of the past 20 years. Income has historically been more than 85% of municipal total return.

When the index yield exceeded 4% over the past 20 years, the subsequent annualized three-year return averaged +6.19%. A 1% fall in yields would theoretically give +11.63% versus -2.34% if yields rise 1%, roughly 5x upside to downside.
Nuveen favors selectively extending duration to 15-25 years given the steep muni yield curve, and prefers high-quality general obligation and essential-service bonds.

Muni inflows are on track for the second-highest annual total on record, over $77 billion year to date. Credit fundamentals are described as sound, supported by income, sales and property tax revenue.
Nuveen is watching the U.S. midterm elections, since 17 states have enacted or proposed property tax relief and several others are considering or have implemented new income taxes.

market_movers.rationale: Alphabet's Q3 cloud growth was extraordinary, but search and advertising results disappointed and free cash flow was negative because of AI buildout costs.

sector_views.rationale: Yields are near historic highs, credit fundamentals are sound and demand is strong. Nuveen calls current entry points compelling.

earnings_insights: Alphabet Q3 (reported, date not given in the note): cloud growth described as extraordinary, search and advertising results disappointing, free cash flow negative. No EPS or revenue figures are given.
Megacap tech capex is expected to keep rising, and investors are questioning AI monetization against the capex.

trade_ideas.description: Add municipal bonds, selectively extending duration to 15-25 years, focused on high-quality general obligation and essential-service bonds
trade_ideas.rationale: Yields are in the 95th percentile of 20 years, the yield curve is steep, fundamentals are sound and demand is strong.
trade_ideas.risk: Rising rates. The note shows a 1% rise in yields implies a -2.34% expected loss.
